title: Rust observation pipeline with unchanged TensorFlow CPU training
conclusion: No measured full-session speedup. Rust took 2.45% longer; retain Python as the default and Rust as an explicit experiment.

final_matched_collection.methodology:
Run matched complete CPU training sessions in an alternating pipeline order.

Includes startup, baseline/before/after evaluation, self-play, held-out validation,
PPO updates, checkpoint writing, model synchronization and shutdown in wall time.
Runs are sequential; do not compile or run other benchmarks alongside them.

notes: Both modes use the same corrected memory accounting and 256 MiB rollout cache; these results are not a comparison against the earlier undercounting cache.

Each final trial has one 64-game self-play round, 8 baseline and before/after evaluation games, 8 engine workers, 2 inference replicas, an 80/20 whole-game holdout, batch 32, 2 PPO epochs and 500 critic steps.

Final self-play game records, initial weights, sample counts and optimizer step counts match across all four trials. Dynamic TensorFlow batching produces small floating-point differences; post-update weights and evaluation outcomes need not be identical.

A separately inspected 392-sample first-round trajectory pair from the prototype had all 14 feature arrays bit-identical; maximum differences were 3.32e-7 in recurrent state, 2.39e-7 in log probabilities and 3.92e-8 in value estimates.
The earlier prototype used Rust padding and cloned the full observation for its canonical fingerprint. Final production batching uses NumPy and fingerprints borrow the JSON values.
Two sequential repeats per mode on this CPU are local evidence, not a confidence interval or a forecast for larger workloads or GPUs.
No external GPU, model architecture, feature vocabulary, game engine pin, rewards or PPO objective was changed.
After the timed jobs ended, only the CLI default/help and an additional native-observation reader lock were changed. The timings do not include this additional lock; the native binary is unchanged.

correctness.exact_parity: Four complete games, both private views, all 14 arrays, history, canonical fingerprints, legal-action ordering, plus a 1,000-decision stochastic walk.
correctness.ownership: Views and slices survive game/observation destruction; cache accounting charges their retained Rust allocation.
correctness.integration: Backend fork/restore/privacy/errors, neural checkpoints, spawned collectors, PPO cache/spill and concurrent update integration checks passed.
